findings.title: Linux socket isolation permits fresh UDP sockets through io_uring
findings.releaseBlockingReason: The active Linux kernel boundary can be bypassed while the tool reports no_network=true, contrary to the explicit tampered-dependency egress guarantee. This does not establish a cryptographic break or an existing malicious dependency.
findings.reproduction: Compile secrets-uring-build.py and execute secrets-uring-run.py on Linux >=5.19 with io_uring enabled. The Rust harness includes the exact unchanged production protect.rs. After isolate(Needs::NOTHING), create an AF_INET/SOCK_DGRAM socket via IORING_OP_SOCKET and send the fixed public marker to a test receiver on 127.0.0.1.
findings.expected: No new network socket can be created by isolated code when no_network is true.
findings.observed: Both protection flags are true; ordinary UdpSocket creation returns EACCES (13). io_uring returns a new socket fd=5, then sendto transmits and the loopback observer receives all 29 synthetic bytes. Product reproduction exits 1.
findings.impact: The seccomp denylist covers socket/socketpair syscalls but io_uring_setup/enter/register are allowed. Landlock restricts TCP bind/connect only, leaving the fresh UDP socket path usable. An attacker already executing code in the process can bypass the promised egress isolation.
findings.recommendedFix: Refuse io_uring_setup, io_uring_enter and io_uring_register in the isolated command filter, or enforce a syscall policy that covers asynchronous socket creation as well as direct calls. Preserve the normal Argon2 and terminal operations and accurately qualify any remaining boundary limitations.
findings.requiredVerification: Under unchanged production isolation, ordinary and io_uring socket attempts must fail on a kernel supporting the operation; run the synthetic loopback reproduction plus normal CLI/Argon2/thread/cancellation regressions. Test egress denial independently of a generic task sandbox.
prerequisites: Native arbitrary-code execution in the isolated process, such as a malicious dependency; ordinary mnemonic input does not trigger this path.
Linux kernel with IORING_OP_SOCKET (5.19+) and an enabled/permitted io_uring facility.
Reachable network required for real remote exfiltration; the audit used loopback only.
findings.limits: No external packet, secret, funding operation or malicious production dependency was used. The host run was a narrow authorized escalation; the ordinary task sandbox receiver EPERM was retained separately. No test of every asynchronous opcode or inherited-descriptor path was performed.

severityHistory.reason: Independent replay confirms failure of the mandatory tampered-dependency egress boundary; AUDIT_STANDARD includes such isolation failures at high. Native code execution remains an explicit prerequisite.

findings.title: Repair API prose promises rejection of damage and cards that the decoder cannot always recognize
findings.releaseBlockingReason: The decoder agrees with the specified bounded-distance behavior; this is a contradictory documentation promise rather than a new cryptographic defect.
findings.reproduction: Shared production crypto API probe: plate A is abandon repeated 23 times plus art (256 zero entropy bits); plate B is abandon repeated 23 times plus diesel (entropy 00...01). repair_words(B, 2) produces minimum uncover. repair(A, cardB) returns B, changing plate word 24 and passing BIP39 checksum. No password or Argon2 call is used.
findings.expected: The specification at mhfe_spec/README.md:694-700 warns that damage beyond the correction bound or a card from another plate can yield a wrong checksum-valid container; success does not authenticate the intended wallet.
findings.observed: API.md says more damage or a card of another plate gives REPAIR_NOT_POSSIBLE, and the public Rust function docs say those cases fail. README.md:464-467 correctly gives the weaker guarantee.
findings.impact: Library consumers may treat successful repair as evidence that the card belongs to the plate or the original was recovered. The public user README already tells the owner to rehearse against a wallet reference.
findings.recommendedFix: Align API.md, its error-code table and repair function rustdoc with the README/spec warning: failure is possible but incorrect checksum-valid output is also possible; successful repair does not authenticate the result.
findings.requiredVerification: Retain the wrong-card example as a documented focused regression, preserve in-bound repair/checksum rejection, and check all three prose locations for the weaker guarantee.

findings.title: Source-check documentation retains obsolete profile-status and passphrase restrictions
findings.releaseBlockingReason: The 24-word profile bytes and public vectors agree; stale profile-status guidance does not change cryptographic outputs.
findings.reproduction: Compare the hash-bound current mhfe README and wallet_check module header with the current local counterpart normative profile section. doc-static-probe.py detects both stale statements.
findings.expected: Current counterpart README.md:574-650 defines the optional draft MHFE-WALLET-CHECK-SEED-1 profile, including domain bytes, BE32(256), PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA512, nonempty/empty passphrase choices and trade-offs.
findings.observed: README says the specification does not define it yet and only its supplement describes it. Public module rustdoc says it is not yet part of the specification, contradicting README.md:313-315 and 333-334 which say other programs following the specification can make/test it. Reference::WalletCheck rustdoc also says its passphrase may not be empty; the current implementation, API.md:108-114 and normative profile all allow the empty-passphrase form.
findings.impact: Readers are directed to research notes instead of the available interoperable byte definition, and cannot tell which statements describe the current profile. The stale Reference comment can lead consumers to reject the supported empty-passphrase form.
findings.recommendedFix: Say that this is the optional draft MHFE-WALLET-CHECK-SEED-1 profile defined by the current specification, and link to its normative section while preserving the experimental and conditioned-entropy warnings. Align Reference::WalletCheck rustdoc with the profile and current API: an empty passphrase is supported, with the explicitly documented one-secret trade-off; mhfe new may still offer the check only for a nonempty passphrase.
findings.requiredVerification: Compare README/rustdoc terminology and links with current mhfe_spec README:572-650; preserve the two matching public digest vectors and declared draft status. Check Reference::WalletCheck with an empty passphrase against the published counter-98918 fixture; do not change the CLI's deliberate narrower generation choice.

findings.title: Packaged browser README links to an absent measurements file
findings.releaseBlockingReason: The broken evidence link does not prevent package loading, encryption, recovery or license redistribution.
findings.reproduction: After the coordinator-built current browser package, read dist/README.md line 84 and test Path(dist/measurements/README.md).exists(): false. All 16 selected local source-document links resolve; this is the sole packaged integration-guide link and it fails. Earlier audit-01 through audit-07 Markdown/JSON were searched for the same published finding and none was found.

findings.title: Dash Platform references accept redundant groups and nonzero Bech32m padding
findings.releaseBlockingReason: Equivalent historical AUD-007-FUN003 classified low/nonblocking; independent wallet data remains correct and no demonstrated fund-loss path. Coordinator owns final disposition.
findings.reproduction: Compile wallet-api-probe.rs against the recorded fresh production rlib; run wallet-independent.py with --root,--probe,--output; run wallet-bech32-reference.mjs against the retained JSON. Expected exactly five mismatches, all Dash.
findings.expected: A 21-byte Dash Platform payload has 34 five-bit groups and two zero padding bits. Extra groups or nonzero residual padding must fail before a wallet comparison.
findings.observed: All five malformed addresses have valid Bech32m checksums, are accepted by Address::parse and match the same valid BIP32 path. Independent @scure/base 2.4.0 separately accepts the checksum and rejects byte conversion for Excess padding or Non-zero padding.
findings.impact: Wallet verification can report a match for a syntactically invalid address supplied as reference. Demonstrated effect is address-validation/interoperability, not different-wallet matching or cryptographic compromise.
findings.recommendedFix: Validate residual padding and the 34-group payload length before converting to 21 bytes; preserve Bech32m/type/network checks.
findings.requiredVerification: Canonical mainnet/testnet and uppercase forms pass;34 groups with any nonzero last two padding bits and extra 35th group fail without a wallet match.

findings.title: Rekey silently ignores an explicit original length for same-length containers
findings.releaseBlockingReason: Bounded defect; no direct secret compromise demonstrated.
findings.reproduction: Run rekey --pim 0 --words 15, answer Yes to the other-wallet warning, then enter the public 12-word same-length-zero-12 container. It asks for Old container password. The same happens for --words 13 or 24 and for 15/18/21-word containers with --words 12. No password was entered; zero Argon2 calls.
findings.expected: A supported selected original length must restrict short-container length, and an unsupported original count must be rejected. mhfe_spec/README.md:535-549 explicitly requires both chosen restrictions to apply before Argon2; CLI option at rekey.rs:38-40 describes original phrase length.
findings.observed: The Suite::SameLength branch returns WordCount::new(container_words) before examining given; six contradictory/invalid options reach the password prompt. With a 24-word suite3 container --words 13 correctly exits 2.
findings.impact: The early input contract is lost and a contrary short container can reach the recovery workflow. The independent wallet/owner confirmation remains mandatory; this probe does not demonstrate bypassing it or wrong-wallet replacement. No cryptographic defect is claimed.
findings.recommendedFix: Validate a supplied WordCount, then require equality for a same-length container; when no length is supplied, derive it from the container as today.
findings.requiredVerification: CLI dispatch or PTY cases for each of 12/15/18/21 short-container lengths with absent/matching/mismatched --words; unsupported 0/13/25; and a suite3 24-word container with permitted chosen source lengths. Prove contradictory lengths reject before reservation/Argon2 and correct cases retain mandatory confirmation.

findings.title: New-wallet phrase formatting frees mnemonic prefixes without wiping
findings.releaseBlockingReason: Best-effort memory hygiene on a local offline computer; no disclosure to another party was demonstrated.
findings.reproduction: Run secrets-format.py. It extracts the exact Zeroizing::new(mnemonic.to_string()) expression from new_wallet.rs and exact reserved phrase_text formatter from phrase.rs; public BIP39 256-bit 0x7f entropy runs under a valid allocator that always moves reallocations.
findings.expected: Program-owned mnemonic text should be written into a reserved Zeroizing buffer so released intermediate allocations do not retain it.
findings.observed: The new-wallet expression releases four heap blocks still containing the public mnemonic prefix legal winner; the reserved production formatter releases zero. The final current expression buffer is wiped, but wrapping it after formatting cannot wipe older growth buffers. Probe exits 1.
findings.impact: Prefixes of a new secret mnemonic can remain in freed process heap memory until reuse or process exit, where swap or a later memory-disclosure bug could observe them. This reintroduces the AUD-005-SEC001 class in a new caller; earlier read_phrase and phrase_from_entropy fixes remain effective.
findings.recommendedFix: Reuse the reserved secret-phrase formatter or construct the phrase in a final-capacity Zeroizing<String> from Mnemonic::words.
findings.requiredVerification: The bounded allocator probe must observe zero current-formatter copies and unchanged public mnemonic text, plus a focused new-wallet formatter regression.
prerequisites: Running mhfe new, checked or unchecked, reaches the formatter.
Allocator may move growing String storage; this is legal behavior rather than a claimed guarantee that every allocator always moves.
findings.limits: The probe executes the exact source expression with the pinned Mnemonic API, not a full interactive new command. It does not test OS swap recovery or compiler/register erasure.
relatedFindings: AUD-005-SEC001: same allocation class, a new CLI caller outside the earlier library fix

findings.title: Hidden-wallet duplicate-detection password copies outlive their memory locks
findings.releaseBlockingReason: A local best-effort anti-swap protection gap; no actual swap disclosure was demonstrated.
findings.reproduction: Run secrets-password-lock.py. It extracts the exact used.push(Zeroizing::new(password.as_bytes().to_vec())) expression, creates sixteen 1024-byte synthetic Password objects, retains their duplicate Vec buffers, drops each original Password and reads kernel VmFlags while duplicates remain alive. No Argon2 is executed.
findings.expected: Every retained normalized password allocation keeps its acquired page-lock protection until it is wiped.
findings.observed: Original Password allocations have locked pages in 16/16 cases. All sixteen retained duplicates remain alive with 0/16 pages locked after original Password drops. The duplicate type has no LockedPages owner. Probe exits 1.
findings.impact: Passwords from earlier hidden wallets remain pageable through the session even if their original lock succeeded. Incidental allocation on another secret locked page can temporarily protect a duplicate, but provides no independent lifetime guarantee. This is distinct from the remedied shared-page refcount defect.
findings.recommendedFix: Retain owning Password values after each successful reveal, or retain an owning zeroizing-and-locked buffer for every duplicate.
findings.requiredVerification: While previous password records remain alive, kernel maps must keep their pages locked after other Password objects drop, subject to documented best-effort mlock failure; duplicate detection and cleanup behavior must remain correct.
prerequisites: A successful hidden-wallet reveal stores a normalized password duplicate.
Continuing the wallets session retains previous duplicates while later prompts and derivations run.
Swap must be enabled and unencrypted for the illustrated anti-swap gap to become disk exposure.
findings.limits: The probe executes the retention expression with the existing library build rather than the entire expensive wallets operation. Actual swap writing/exfiltration is not shown.

findings.title: Private-screen guard accepts stdout and stderr connected to different terminals
findings.releaseBlockingReason: Requires explicit descriptor redirection to separate terminals; public output routing and the new-command guard were reproduced, without creating or exposing a real wallet.
findings.reproduction: Launch repair-words --count 4 with stdin and stderr on PTY A, stdout on separate PTY B, TERM=xterm-256color and NO_COLOR=1. Type the public zero-12 suite3 container. At the clear-screen wait press Escape. Separately launch new with the same descriptors and stop at its first settings question; do not generate a mnemonic or run Argon2.
findings.expected: The private-only guard binds phrase output to the terminal controlled by the alternate-screen and clear sequences, or refuses a different output terminal before asking any input.
findings.observed: Repair exits 0 and restores input settings, but numbered public repair words remain on PTY B. PTY B receives no enter-alternate-screen or leave/clear sequence. All such controls and the clear-screen promise are on PTY A. new accepts this layout and reaches the settings question even though its refusal text requires no output redirected. The same-terminal repair control enters, clears and leaves the private screen correctly.
findings.impact: A user deliberately or accidentally redirecting stdout to a second TTY may leave secret-result output on that other terminal main screen and its scrollback despite the private-screen promise. The probe used only public repair words, and the new probe stopped before entropy generation. This does not demonstrate a normal single-terminal leak, unauthorized remote access, or real-wallet compromise.
findings.recommendedFix: Verify that stdout and the stream carrying terminal controls refer to the same terminal before claiming private output, with a safe platform-specific identity check; otherwise refuse private-only commands or use one terminal stream consistently for secret display and its controls. Preserve explicitly requested script output contracts.
findings.requiredVerification: Two-PTY regressions for new/wallets refusal before input and public repair/decrypt output routing; single-PTY alternate-screen and clearing controls; redirected pipe/file/script cases; and equivalent native Windows console-handle behavior.
findings.limits: Only public repair-word output persistence and new's early guard acceptance were executed. Later new/wallet secret-output persistence is a source-traced implication, not a generated-phrase runtime reproduction. No real secret was exposed.

findings.title: Narrow terminal menu redraw leaves stale rows and multiple selection markers
findings.releaseBlockingReason: Presentation ambiguity at narrow widths; no incorrect command dispatch or loss of cryptographic correctness demonstrated.
findings.reproduction: Start the actual target/release/mhfe with stdin/stdout/stderr on one capable PTY, NO_COLOR=1, 60 or 40 columns and 100 rows. Wait for Esc quits, then send Down. The harness reconstructs physical menu rows from retained actual PTY output; tall height removes scrolling as a confounder.
findings.expected: The menu redraw replaces the old list and displays exactly one selected entry, consistent with arrow-key navigation.
findings.observed: At both 60 and 40 columns, wrapped entries take additional physical rows but the child redraw sends cursor-up 13. The old highlighted entry 1 survives above the new list while entry 2 is highlighted there. The derived grids contain two selection markers. The 80-column control has one. Escape exits 0 and restores termios at all three widths.
findings.impact: Users of narrow terminal windows can see stale options and two conflicting selection indicators. Internal selection remains a single index; this evidence does not show wrong-command execution or secret exposure.
findings.recommendedFix: Use the actual terminal width when rendering and counting physical rows, including hints and explanations, or fall back to non-redrawing numbered input below a supported minimum width. Account for resize between draws.
findings.requiredVerification: Retain 80-column control and 60/40-column PTY cases with one marker after repeated Up/Down, correct selected dispatch, clean Escape return, and representative short heights and terminal resizing. A real terminal visual check should supplement the text reconstruction.

remediation.result: Enabled host io_uring_setup succeeds before isolation; all three io_uring syscalls and socket/socketpair return EACCES under actual production isolation. Four workers start, inherit the namespace and filters, and join. Reduced-cost native encryption/recovery and loopback serve remain functional; inherited-descriptor claims were qualified.
Wrong repair card is independently reproduced yielding another checksum-valid plate. API prose, error table and rustdoc now describe bounded correction without authentication.

Optional source-profile status and empty-passphrase API agree with the current counterpart. Both complete public digests and crossed negative controls reproduce independently; the narrower CLI offer is retained.

Existing browser build produces the current guide in dist. Its measurement reference is an explicit repository URL with a retained local target; all seven runtime checksums agree. Both browser Argon2 build modes pass reduced-cost package checks.
All original five malformed Dash aliases and uppercase forms are rejected; canonical controls pass. Independent mainnet/testnet, case, padding, extra-group and path-boundary challenge passes 34/34.

browser.kind: informational observation; no new finding ID
browser.title: Inactive WASM stack copies can retain a synthetic round key after source-level moves
browser.interpretation: Every marker starts only in the injected synthetic key, outside WASM. Engine throw before round_values returns wipes the callback view and leaves no marker. After successful return, marker copies persist below the restored stack pointer (1048576), while the sampled heap allocation is 1245192. This is consistent with inactive compiler stack copies associated with RoundValues return/moves, not a demonstrated abandoned heap owner or missed final Drop.
browser.source: src/feistel.rs:160-171 creates and returns RoundValues; :191-198 derives Zeroize and ZeroizeOnDrop. SECURITY.md:35-40 and docs/API.md:137-140 already state compiler/register/stack limits. web/client.js:257-265, :309-319 ends the whole worker on result/error/cancel.
browser.impactAndLimits: The known key pattern can be inspected in a directly retained low-level WASM instance. The normal package discards the operation worker at completion or cancellation. No disclosure path, compiler-generated copy elimination, OS physical erasure or actual Argon2 key residue was tested.
browser.classification: Retain as bounded evidence of an existing documented limitation. No new confirmed defect or release blocker.
